Our Second Century

our focus

A Strategic Vision

President Vincent Price leads the Duke community with a compelling vision for advancing both the university and the world over the next century.

look ahead

Empower the Boldest Thinkers

Duke is the place where the world’s brightest minds come to meet the most important challenges. We recognize that their accomplishments comprise the true measure of our institutional excellence.

Transform Teaching and Learning

Duke is rethinking our undergraduate, graduate, and professional education strategy, taking advantage of new technological opportunities, and building a responsive, team-based learning community that includes everyone.

Strengthen Our Campus Community

Working to ensure that all who call Duke home share a lived experience that is increasingly inclusive, equitable, engaging, healthy and vibrant. Duke seeks to be a diverse and stimulating campus that promotes personal growth among all of our students, faculty, staff, and visitors.

Partner With Purpose

Strengthening relationships in Durham and serve as a collaborative catalyst in our region to our research ecosystem while improving community health, housing, and education.

Engage a Global Network

Activating our alumni and engaging our friends to create new opportunities for growth and discovery to advance our educational, research, and service missions.

Our Climate Commitment

sustainability

Collaboration and Community

The Duke Climate Commitment encompasses the full breadth of the University — every school, center and institute on our campuses has a role in our work to develop and implement climate solutions.

join us

As we chart our course for the next century, the Duke Climate Commitment is essential to our vision. This university-wide initiative addresses the climate crisis by fostering sustainable and equitable solutions for a resilient, carbon-neutral world.

– Vincent Price, President

Our First 100 Years

Duke wasn’t always Duke. What started as a small school two hours west of Durham has grown in incredible ways.

What is 100 Years?

Established in 1924 in Durham, North Carolina, Duke University is one of the world’s leading institutions for education, research, and patient care. Take a look at Duke’s 100 year history as we reflect on the moments that made us.

A Centennial of Progress

The captivating story of the founding of Duke University tells of grand dreams and progressive ideals, but it is only one of Duke’s stories.

In 2024 we celebrated the one hundred years since Trinity College became Duke University. See a few of the highlights in this gallery or visit 100.duke.edu to relive the celebration.

Permanent Good: A Duke Documentary chronicles the evolution of Duke University from a one-room schoolhouse to one of the world’s preeminent institutions of higher learning, bringing to life the moments and people that forged this path.

Duke Decades are visual deep dives through the archives exploring Duke’s first 100 years through historical photos and videos, one decade at a time.

Centennial Spotlights look back at the people who contributed to Duke’s meteoric rise and the trajectory they helped to set for the university.

Then & Now vividly shows the changes that have happened across campus over the past hundred years.

Leadership

Our institutional culture is built upon our history and values. Our shared values—respect, trust, inclusion, discovery and excellence—are more than aspirations. They are the beliefs and behaviors that we expect of ourselves and of our colleagues.

President

Vincent Price

Vincent Price is the 10th President of Duke University, where he is also Walter Hines Page Professor of Public Policy and Political Science in the Sanford School of Public Policy and Trinity College of Arts & Sciences. A leading global expert on public opinion, social influence, and political communication and former editor-in-chief of Public Opinion Quarterly, President Price came to Duke in 2017. Since arriving on campus, he has turned his attention to the future of the university, developing a strategic vision focused on five core principles: empowering people, transforming education, building community, forging partnerships, and engaging a global network.

Duke’s Values

At Duke, our values are more than words. They shape how we learn, work, and lead. Built on respect, trust, inclusion, discovery, and excellence, these values guide our community and influence how we honor our past while preparing for the future.

How We Lead at Duke

The Duke Endowment

The Duke Endowment is a private foundation established in 1924 that strengthens communities
in North and South Carolina by funding initiatives in child and family well-being, health care, and higher education.
